chapter: Europe and the Black and Blue years
title: Why Black and Blue records are good but pay no royalties
summary: Dance admires how Black and Blue records unsaleable artists on good tours, but Humes says they send no royalties. She mentions a Hot Club of France award.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well listen Helen, you know what I think is absolutely remarkable, and that is, all the records they put out are good, all their records are good. And they put out people, you know, that everybody here says, there's no money in them. Well, you know, like Jay or different people like that. They put all these different people together and they put their tours together and then they record their tours. And those records are always good. All of them are good. And yet

they are records you can't persuade people here to make. Let's say Harry Lim, and you say Harry, they may sound wonderful together. No, nothing happens. You can't sell them and yet they can sell them and they make wonderful records.
Yeah. But they don't send you No royalties.
Oh, there's a catch to it then. They've had Grammy nominations. And
The Hot Jazz, and I got a thing for that, an award.
Oh you did. Was that from Hugues Panassie, The Hot Club of France.
